title: A future connection to primes
narration: There is a genuine bridge to primes: explicit formulas connect weighted prime counts with zeta zeros. Our proposed next experiment would reconstruct that count from finitely many zeros and certify the omitted error. A useful result would be a rigorously bounded approximation to prime distribution.
formulaLines: RH ⇒ ψ(x) = x + O(√x log² x),  x → ∞
bullets: Schematic bridge: ψ = x − ∑ρ x^ρ/ρ + corrections.
Zeros oscillate in log x; RH fixes β = 1/2.
Future: compare with sieve-computed ψ; certify E.
bubble: Connect the zero patterns to a measurable prime function.
visual: Editable symbolic arrows connect actual zeta zeros at target a=0 to oscillations in log x, then to a weighted prime-power staircase. Mark every illustrative reconstruction PROPOSED, not measured. Never feed nonzero-target a-points into the zero sum. Show no newly computed curve or certificate.

composition.placement: After the four frozen formal scenes and before the repository card
composition.note: This supplemental composition overrides only production timing; neither frozen formulation file is edited.

definitions.psi: For real x>1, psi(x)=sum over prime p and integers k>=1 with p^k<=x of log p. Equivalently sum_{n<=x} Lambda(n), with Lambda(p^k)=log p and Lambda(n)=0 otherwise. Natural logarithms are used. This weights prime powers; it is not the ordinary count pi(x).
definitions.rho: rho=beta+i*gamma ranges over actual nontrivial zeros of zeta, counted with multiplicity. These are target-a=0 zeros, not solutions of zeta(s)=a for a!=0.
definitions.powerConvention: For real x>1, x^rho=exp(rho*log x), so x^rho=x^beta exp(i*gamma*log x). The phase winds in log x. Conjugate zeros combine into real oscillatory contributions.

exactFormula.status: established theorem; not newly proved or implemented here
exactFormula.domain: Real noninteger x>1. This deliberately avoids every integer jump location.
exactFormula.summation: Symmetric height cutoff, all nontrivial zeros with multiplicity; no arbitrary rearrangement or absolute-convergence claim.
exactFormula.jumpConvention: At a prime power x=p^k, the standard midpoint version uses psi_0(x)=(psi(x-)+psi(x))/2=psi(x)-(log p)/2. The displayed exact formula here is restricted to nonintegers, so it makes no endpoint assignment at a jump. A future implementation must select and state its jump convention.

rhConditionalEstimate.statement: If RH holds, psi(x)=x+O(sqrt(x)*(log x)^2) as x tends to infinity.
rhConditionalEstimate.meaning: There exist constants C and x0 such that |psi(x)-x|<=C*sqrt(x)*(log x)^2 for x>=x0. This does not assert RH, provide the numerical constant for a new program, or bound the error of an arbitrary finite zero sum.

elementaryRelations: psi(x)=sum_{k>=1} theta(x^(1/k)); only finitely many terms are nonzero.
pi(x)=theta(x)/log x + integral from 2 to x of theta(u)/(u*(log u)^2) du, for x>=2.
For integer n>=1, p_n=min{m in integers, m>=2: pi(m)>=n}.
countingAndNthPrime.derivation: The first identity groups prime powers. The second follows by writing 1/log p=1/log x+integral_p^x du/(u*(log u)^2), multiplying by log p, and summing over primes. The last is the definition of the nth jump of pi.
countingAndNthPrime.scope: These connect prime distribution and counting to prime locations. A bounded approximation does not identify an exact nth prime unless its counting bounds isolate the relevant jump; no such solver is proposed as the present deliverable.

proposedBoundedExperiment.status: future work; no reconstruction or certified truncation bound has been implemented here
proposedBoundedExperiment.objective: Construct a finite-zero approximation Psi_T on a fixed finite test domain and prove explicit total errors E(x,T), then independently compare with a sieve-computed weighted prime-power sum.
proposedBoundedExperiment.initialTestDomain: Suggested exact grid x=j+1/2 for integers j=2,...,100; it avoids jump ambiguities. Freeze the chosen grid, height cutoff T and desired error tolerance before evaluating success.
proofObligations: Certify all zeros included below the cutoff, their multiplicities, and numerical enclosures; prove completeness up to T rather than using a selected visual sample.

Derive an explicit remainder for omitted zeros with its exact x/T restrictions; bound evaluation and zero-location errors separately. Never treat the conditional RH estimate for psi-x as a finite-sum tail bound.
Handle jumps or use a precisely specified smoothing and separately bound the smoothing error.
Compare with an independently enumerated prime-power sum using rigorous logarithm enclosures; store replayable inequalities |psi(x)-Psi_T(x)|<=E(x,T).
proposedBoundedExperiment.passFail: Pass only when all declared error inequalities are certified and the independent values lie in the enclosures. A smaller empirical discrepancy without a tail proof is numerical evidence only; inability to certify remains an open obligation.
proposedBoundedExperiment.connectionToCurrentTool: The phase/origin visualizer can inspect how individual genuine-zero contributions combine. The accepted continuation experiment supplies no complete zero table or prime reconstruction certificate.
proposedBoundedExperiment.noveltyAndRhLimit: Explicit formulas and finite-zero reconstructions are established methods. This proposed experiment makes no originality, improved algorithm, new RH bound, or RH-proof claim.

sources.title: NIST DLMF 25.16(i), Distribution of Primes
sources.use: Definition of psi and its zero connection. Its displayed RH error is O(x^(1/2+epsilon)) for every epsilon>0, not the sharper log-squared form.
